paper.title: Effect of annealing temperature on the microstructure and tensile properties of Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel
paper.paper_scope: Investigates the microstructure evolution and tensile properties of a single Mn-lean Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel (Fe–Mn–Al–C) annealed at 700–1200 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching, examining how annealing temperature governs the α/γ/κ-carbide phase fractions, grain size, and the resulting strength–ductility balance.

alloys.description: A low-density high-strength Fe–Mn–Al–C steel designed to have a relatively low Mn content (10 wt.%) together with a high Al content (10 wt.%) and 0.7 wt.% C; prepared as a 20 kg ingot by vacuum induction melting to study microstructure and tensile properties after annealing at various temperatures.
alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C (wt.%). Measured composition of the hot-rolled steel: 10.4 wt.% Mn, 9.7 wt.% Al, 0.70 wt.% C, Fe balance. Measured density about 6.80 g/cm³, about 13% lower than pure Fe. The chemical composition is given in wt.%.

processes.description: 20 kg ingot forged, homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h, then hot-rolled to a 3 mm thick plate with finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C, followed by water quenching to about 300 °C (reference state before annealing).
processes.processes_notes: This hot-rolled + water-quenched plate is the common precursor for all subsequent annealing treatments.

unmapped_findings: A Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase diagram calculation (database TCFE7) was performed for the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel, predicting κ-carbide formation by eutectoid reaction γ→α+κ below about 823 °C; the steel is not in equilibrium so measured phase fractions/dissolution temperature differ from the calculation (b0022, b0033, b0052).

Table 2 compares tensile properties of the present Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel with literature Fe–Mn–Al–C steels (Fe-28Mn-10Al-1.0C, Fe-20Mn-9Al-0.6C, Fe-18Mn-10Al-1.2C, Fe-18Mn-10Al-0.8C, Fe-12Mn-8.0Al-0.8C); these literature steels are cited comparisons, not research objects of this study (b0071, b0072, b0073).

Study methods: phase identification by XRD (Cu target, 40 kV/150 mA), OM, FE-SEM (20 kV) with EDS, and TEM (200 kV); phase volume fractions determined from XRD by the direct comparison method; room-temperature tensile tests at initial strain rate 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ with tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction (b0017, b0018).
